"Absurd", which the group debuted onstage at Fenway Park a few days earlier, was released as a single on August 6, 2021, its first new material since 2008. "Hard Skool" followed on September 24, and both singles are reworkings of songs from the Chinese Democracy sessions. A physical release of "Hard Skool" was announced as both an EP and a vinyl single with different track listings; the EP, featuring "Absurd" and live tracks, came out on February 25, 2022. Slash said later in 2021 that the group had been reworking Chinese-era songs for future release, and in 2022 he confirmed that more new songs were in the works, saying "There's new Guns material coming out as we speak, and we'll probably keep putting it out until the entire record's worth of stuff is done".
A remastered deluxe box set of the two Illusion albums, Use Your Illusion (Super Deluxe Edition), was announced on September 20, 2022, and released on November 11. It includes both albums remastered, two live concerts from 1991 (New York) and 1992 (Las Vegas), a Blu-ray of the New York concert, and photographs and memorabilia. A live version of "You Could Be Mine" served as the lead single.
The Guns N' Roses 2023 Tour included the group's first headlining set at Glastonbury Festival, on June 24. It drew mixed reviews, with some publications calling it one of the worst headlining sets in festival history, and the group responded by claiming that technical difficulties had resulted in a poor mix. The piano-driven single "Perhaps" followed on August 18, 2023, with its "R-side" "The General" released digitally and on vinyl on December 8.

Lineup changes and 2026 world tour
The "Because What You Want & What You Get Are Two Completely Different Things Tour" was announced in December 2024. Its 2025 dates took the group through Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Latin America, including stops in Düsseldorf, Riyadh, and Mumbai.
Longtime drummer Frank Ferrer, who had joined in 2006, left on March 19, 2025. Isaac Carpenter was announced as his replacement the next day. Carpenter made his live debut with the group on May 1.
On July 5, 2025, the group played several Black Sabbath covers at Black Sabbath's farewell concert, Back to the Beginning. A remastered Live Era '87–'93 was announced in October and released on vinyl on November 21.
On November 24, 2025, GNR announced a 2026 world tour alongside two new songs, "Nothin'" and "Atlas", originally scheduled for release on December 2. The songs were released on December 4. Like the group's other post-reunion singles, both date to the Chinese Democracy sessions and feature new parts from Slash and McKagan. In early 2026, Slash and McKagan both mentioned the band finished releasing reworked songs and the plan was to release them as a package at some point, with Slash saying, "the next record that we're gonna do is gonna be all new original stuff and that'll be an actual album."
On March 27, 2026, the day before the tour began, the group announced that Melissa Reese would not be joining it "due to unforeseen personal reasons". No replacement was named.
The tour opened on March 28 at the Tecate Pa'l Norte festival in Monterrey, Mexico, where "Nothin'" and "Atlas" received their first live performances. It continued with a Brazil leg in April and dates across Europe, before a North American stadium run opened on July 23 at Carter-Finley Stadium in Raleigh, North Carolina, with support from acts including the Black Crowes, Public Enemy, and Ice Cube. As of October 2026, the tour is scheduled to continue through Asia and Oceania, with dates in India, Indonesia, Singapore, Australia, and New Zealand ending on December 17.

Legacy
Guns N' Roses signed with Geffen Records in 1986. Their debut album, Appetite for Destruction, released in July 1987, debuted at number 182 on the Billboard 200 and reached number one on August 6, 1988, after incessant touring and MTV airplay of "Sweet Child o' Mine" and "Paradise City"; it then spent 52 consecutive weeks in the top ten. The album was certified 18× platinum by the RIAA in September 2008, making it the best-selling debut album in the United States until Cracked Rear View by Hootie & the Blowfish surpassed it in 2018. It has sold more than 30 million copies worldwide. Apple Music said "Despite only releasing four album's [sic] worth of original material in their original incarnation, GNR had burned so brightly in such a short time that their legend remains stubbornly intact".
Appetite for Destruction is credited with "(changing) hard rock's sensibilities at the time", and bringing a "danger, attitude and legitimacy" to rock, leading to a decline in the late-'80s glam metal craze. The band has also been credited with helping re-popularize power ballads in heavy metal music.

We didn't have illusions that we were going to be huge or anything. But people started coming to our gigs and then labels started coming to our gigs and we made the record we wanted to make. And, all of a sudden, it hit, and it seems like a whole generation of the world had an affinity for that record.

Rankings and honors
Appetite for Destruction was ranked 62nd on Rolling Stone's 2012 list of "The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time". In 2004, Rolling Stone ranked the band No. 92 on its list of the "100 Greatest Artists of All Time". The television network VH1 ranked Guns N' Roses ninth in its "100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock" special, and 32nd on its "100 Greatest Artists of All Time". In 2002, Q named the band in its list of the "50 Bands to See Before You Die". "Paradise City" was voted ninth-best hard rock song out of 100 candidates by VH1.
Individual members have also been ranked highly. Rolling Stone placed Rose 64th on its 2008 list of the 100 greatest singers, while Time named Slash runner-up to Jimi Hendrix on its 2009 list of the ten greatest electric guitar players and Rolling Stone ranked him 65th among the 100 greatest guitarists in 2011. McKagan was included on MusicRadar's 2017 list of the 50 best bassists of all time, and Stradlin appeared on Ultimate Guitar's lists of the best rhythm guitarists, while Adler was ranked 98th on Rolling Stone's list of the greatest drummers. Later members were also ranked among the best in their field: keyboardist Dizzy Reed ranked among the greatest rock pianists by IRockU, drummer Matt Sorum ranked among the best rock drummers by Drum!, guitarist Buckethead was ranked among the fastest and most innovative contemporary guitarists by publications such as AllMusic and Guitar World, and studio drummer Josh Freese ranked among the top 10 rock drummers by Gibson.
The band won the American Music Awards for favorite heavy metal/hard rock artist and album (Appetite for Destruction) in January 1990, and won favorite heavy metal/hard rock artist again in January 1992. "Sweet Child o' Mine" won the MTV Video Music Awards for Best Heavy Metal Video in 1989, and at the 1992 ceremony the band received the Video Vanguard Award and "November Rain" won for Best Cinematography. The band has received Grammy Award nominations but has not won one; in March 2024, Appetite for Destruction was announced as one of ten recordings inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
Guns N' Roses was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame on April 14, 2012, in its first year of eligibility, with Green Day presenting the induction. The group is one of the world's best-selling bands of all time, having sold more than 100 million records worldwide, including shipments of 45 million in the United States. The Not in This Lifetime... Tour (2016–2019) grossed $584.2 million from more than 5.3 million tickets, making it the third-highest-grossing tour in Billboard Boxscore history when it ended. The video for "Sweet Child o' Mine" was the first from the 1980s to reach one billion YouTube views, in October 2019, and "November Rain" was the first from the 1990s to do so, in 2018.

Musical style
Early Guns N' Roses music was a fusion of punk rock, blues rock, hard rock, heavy metal, and glam metal. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame describes the band as combining a reverence for classic rock acts with the abrasiveness of metal and the anti-authoritarianism of punk, rising from the Sunset Strip scene of the 1980s. The Illusion albums saw the band branching out into art rock and incorporating influences from progressive rock, folk rock, progressive metal, speed metal, funk metal, and industrial music. "The Spaghetti Incident?" saw the group cover mostly punk rock songs. Since its 1999 revival, the band has retained hard rock and piano rock features while including elements of industrial rock, electronic rock, nu metal, industrial metal and trip hop. In the 1990s, the band integrated keyboards (played by either Rose or Reed) into its sound. Teddy Andreadis was brought in as an additional keyboardist and harmonica player for the Use Your Illusion Tour, alongside multiple backing vocalists and a brass and woodwind section. Later tours saw keyboardist Chris Pitman (and after 2016, Melissa Reese) contribute sub-bass and synth parts, as well as reproducing the brass and string parts of songs electronically.
The Finnish band Hanoi Rocks heavily influenced both the image and sound of Guns N' Roses; singer Michael Monroe and Rose have collaborated on several occasions. Rose has stated that the band was massively influenced by groups like Queen, AC/DC, the Rolling Stones, Aerosmith, and Rose Tattoo, and that the sound of Appetite for Destruction was influenced by AC/DC, Led Zeppelin, the Who, Cheap Trick, Aerosmith, Van Halen, the New York Dolls, and Hanoi Rocks. The band was also influenced by Black Sabbath, the Sex Pistols, T. Rex, MC5, and Accept. Rose's orchestral-style songwriting on the Illusion albums was influenced by the Electric Light Orchestra, Elton John, and Queen, particularly their album Queen II. Rose cited the influence of Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" in recording the title track of Chinese Democracy. Rose was heavily influenced by the industrial rock sound of Nine Inch Nails, changing the band's sound in the lead up to Chinese Democracy. Critics noted influences of Queen, Elton John, Wings and Andrew Lloyd Webber on some songs on Chinese Democracy.

Influence on other artists
Several established musicians have praised the band. Joe Perry stated that the band was the first to remind him of Led Zeppelin. Ozzy Osbourne said that the band could have been "the next Rolling Stones" if the classic lineup had stayed together. Tom Petty also favorably compared the band to the Rolling Stones. Country musician Steve Earle told Rolling Stone that "Guns N' Roses are what every L.A. band pretends to be". Kiss bassist Gene Simmons named Appetite for Destruction among his thirteen favorite albums of all time, saying it had an honesty that rock and roll had been missing. Queen guitarist Brian May, who played with the band on its 1993 tour, said he felt a "spiritual connection" between Guns N' Roses and Queen. Gangsta rap group N.W.A., of whom Guns N' Roses were early supporters and befriended, named a song "Appetite for Destruction" after the Guns album of the same name.
The band has influenced many later rock acts. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame lists Buckcherry, Avenged Sevenfold, The Darkness, Wolfmother, Greta Van Fleet, The Pretty Reckless, My Chemical Romance and The Strokes among the artists it influenced. Avenged Sevenfold's M. Shadows has called Guns N' Roses his favorite band of all time, saying his father gave him Appetite for Destruction when it came out, and the band immersed itself in the album, along with Metallica's Black Album, before recording Hail to the King. The Welsh band Manic Street Preachers have cited the band as a major influence on their debut album Generation Terrorists: guitarist James Dean Bradfield taught himself guitar by playing along to Appetite for Destruction, and the group covered "It's So Easy" as a B-side to their 1992 single "You Love Us". Queensrÿche vocalist Todd La Torre called Appetite for Destruction "a very influential album for me". Slipknot frontman Corey Taylor has called Guns N' Roses "my Rolling Stones", saying Appetite for Destruction was the one album that his metal, punk, skater and hard rock friends could all agree on. Pantera drummer Vinnie Paul recalled the album's impact on its release as "huge". Other acts reported to have been influenced by the band include Black Label Society, Bullet for My Valentine, Fall Out Boy, Fozzy, Hinder, Shinedown, and Sum 41.

In popular culture
Guns N' Roses have appeared in popular culture across television, film, and video games. Arrested Development featured a gag in the episode "Sword of Destiny" (2005), where Tony Wonder attempts to name his magic DVD "Use Your Illusion". Slash was lampooned in the South Park episode "Crack Baby Athletic Association", where he is portrayed as a mythical figure named "Vunter Slaush", a Santa Claus-like legend believed by the children. Celebrity Deathmatch staged a fight between Axl Rose and Slash in a music-themed episode. Rose also voiced himself in a 2018 episode of New Looney Tunes, and in 2021 appeared in Scooby-Doo and Guess Who?. Can't Hardly Wait (1998) features a comedic performance of "Paradise City", while Step Brothers (2008) includes the family car singalong of "Sweet Child o' Mine". The U.S. release of the video game Mega Man X5 (2000) renamed its bosses after Guns N' Roses members. The manga series JoJo's Bizarre Adventure part The JoJoLands introduced a Stand named "November Rain" after the Guns N' Roses song. "Welcome to the Jungle", frequently played at sporting events, is considered a sports anthem.

Criticism and controversies
Guns N' Roses has received criticism throughout the years. The band received criticism for drug and alcohol use in the 1980s and early 1990s. Songs such as "One in a Million" and the band's cover of Charles Manson's "Look at Your Game, Girl" were considerably controversial upon release. In addition, some lyrics have been regarded as sexist. The band has also been criticized for tardiness and starting shows later than advertised. The long periods of time between albums are another source of criticism.
Several fellow musicians were also critical of the band. Nirvana frontman Kurt Cobain stated that his band was "not your typical Guns N' Roses type of band that has absolutely nothing to say" and refused to tour with them. When the band and Living Colour both supported the Rolling Stones at the Los Angeles Coliseum in 1989, Living Colour guitarist Vernon Reid publicly criticized "One in a Million" during his band's set, leading to a public exchange between Reid and Rose. Faith No More, who opened for the band on its 1992 stadium tour, openly mocked Rose in interviews and on stage, and singer Mike Patton later said the band had been treated poorly by Guns N' Roses. Rose also feuded publicly with Mötley Crüe singer Vince Neil following a dispute between Neil and Stradlin. Despite his admiration for Appetite for Destruction, Corey Taylor has said he has no respect for performers who keep fans waiting two to three hours, a criticism he directed at Rose. The band's 1992 co-headlining stadium tour with Metallica was marred by tension; Metallica members criticized Rose's behavior and late performances.
The group's live performances have occasionally ended in violence, most famously the 1991 Riverport Riot in St. Louis, when Rose leapt into the crowd to confront a fan with a camera before shutting down the show. His departure from the stage sparked chaos that injured dozens and caused extensive property damage, leading to lawsuits and Rose's arrest. In October 2009, Ulrich Schnauss's record labels Independiente and Domino sued Guns N' Roses, alleging that the band had committed copyright infringement by using portions of Schnauss's compositions in the track "Riad N' the Bedouins" on the album Chinese Democracy. The band claimed the samples were obtained legitimately. Chinese Democracy was banned in the People's Republic of China, due to criticism in its title track of the Government of the People's Republic of China and reference to the Falun Gong. The Chinese government said through the media that it "turns its spear point on China". In November 2023, former band photographer Katarina Benzova filed a lawsuit alleging that the band had falsely claimed ownership of photographs she took, and that manager Fernando Lebeis had subjected her to repeated unwanted advances over the twelve years she worked for the band.
